links.outcome: LLM reasoning accuracy on Written Exposure Therapy questions when authoritative guideline passages are provided via RAG
links.effect: Errors persisted even when authoritative passages were provided; RAG can constrain outputs, but reasoning must be assessed as rigorously as retrieval. No numbers reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Our results highlight both the potential and the risks: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can constrain outputs, but safe deployment requires assessing reasoning as rigorously as retrieval.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating accuracy, consistency, and fidelity of LLM reasoning over retrieved clinical protocol passages

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM reasoning errors and the impact/limitations of RAG retrieval-grounding with clinical guidelines (Written Exposure Therapy protocols).
